CatalystMap

● LIVE

Full-stack app mapping high-attention companies to listed suppliers. Relationships are typed, source-cited and scored 0–100 by a deterministic formula, with an AI-assisted research workflow gated by human curator approval. Server-side compute, caching, append-only audit trail.

DART Disclosure Alert Bot

● RUNNING

Monitors Korea’s DART filings, filters supply-contract & facility-investment keywords, and sends weekday Telegram alerts with Claude-written summaries and a 6-point risk score. SQLite dedupes filings and tracks recurring patterns.

Removes — Monitoring friction

ThreadMate

● SHIPPED

A Chrome extension that finds who quietly unfollowed you by diffing only what’s already on screen — no private APIs, no servers, nothing leaves the browser. Privacy as a hard constraint.

Removes — Social friction
JavaScriptChrome ExtensionDOM DiffingPrivacy-first

Security Controls Labs

● LAB

Hardened a virtualised Windows environment, then ran controlled penetration testing — msfvenom reverse-TCP payload → Meterpreter → privilege escalation — mapping each attack path back to a defensive control. Designed S3 with versioning, lifecycle, SSE and IAM least-privilege.

Removes — Exposure friction

EMILY JO

SYSTEMS BUILDER · REMOVES FRICTION FOR A LIVING · LV.21

I build systems that remove unnecessary friction. Every project starts the same way: I hit something tedious or broken, get annoyed that it still works this way — then build the fix instead of complaining about it. I think in systems. I’d rather spend a week making a problem never happen again than an hour doing it by hand, and the part I chase is the moment friction disappears and something that used to be hard just runs itself.

The cyber-security background is where the rigor comes from — evidence over opinion, audit trails, assume it can break. The record below is real, but it’s the second thing about me, not the first.
